articles.title: Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua Fight Details Confirmed, Location, Date for Netflix Bout Revealed
articles.summary: The highly anticipated heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua is official.
articles.body:
The highly anticipated heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua is official.

After Chris McKenna of The Athletic reported the bout was in the works for Dec. 11, Ring Magazine officially announced on Thursday that Fury and Joshua will square off on Dec. 11 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff with Netflix broadcasting the event.

One potentially interesting note is there was no start time listed, which has been a topic of discussion when the fight was being rumored.

ESPN's James Dielhenn reported that Matchroom's Eddie Hearn, who represents Joshua, "all but confirmed the dream fight is close to being agreed" upon for the Dec. 11 date. To maximize the worldwide audience on Netflix, Hearn added that the fight will start later than usual, but not as late as some fans fear.

"People talk about a 3 a.m. BST [10 p.m. ET] fight? I don't think you'll see the fight that late," Hearn said. "But obviously there had to be conversations with the stadium about what's possible and what is not possible. That's probably a reason for the delay [of the official announcement] -- to make sure everything is boxed off with the council to have a slightly later start time."

Fury and Joshua signed contracts in April to face each other later this year, but months of contentious negotiations created concerns over whether their long-awaited fight would ever come to fruition. It sounds like things are moving in the right direction, as Hearn indicated that he and Joshua are satisfied with the current plans.

"Over the past week or two, we made our decision. AJ was the guy leading that decision," Hearn said. "We weren't interested in accepting extra money or changing the terms of the agreement to change the location. He wanted to make sure the fight was in the UK. Since then, they have accepted that. We are working together and speaking to Netflix to lock in the date. I think the date is locked in."

Fury has rebounded following his back-to-back losses against Oleksandr Usyk in 2024. The 38-year-old defeated Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach earlier this year, bringing his career record to 36-2-1.

Since dropping the IBF heavyweight title to Daniel Dubois, Joshua has scored knockout wins over Jake Paul and Kristian Prenga. He is 30-4 with 27 knockouts in 34 career fights.

articles.standfirst: Tras imponerse en semifinales a la alemana Maxi Klozer
articles.summary: Tras imponerse en semifinales a la alemana Maxi Klozer
articles.body: Laura Fuertes, que un día antes hizo historia al asegurar la primera medalla española de una boxeadora en un Europeo, ha dado un paso más este miércoles. La asturiana ha sellado el billete para la final continental de menos de 51 kilos tras imponerse en las semifinales a la alemana Maxi Klozer por decisión dividida (3-2). La gijonesa fue superior a la germana y supo mantener el control y la iniciativa a lo largo de todo el combate. Su forma de manejar la distancia, unida a su ventaja de altura y envergadura, resultaron determinantes para llevarse la victoria. Será el tercer podio de 2026 tras la lesión. Primero fue en un codo, y después la fractura en la falange del meñique derecho por la que tuvo que ser operada hace nueve meses. Ya en junio, se colgó el bronce en la Copa del Mundo de Guiyang (China). Entonces reconocía que había sido un "proceso raro y largo". Desde la operación no encontraba volver a ser yo encima del ring y volver a encontrar mis ritmos y mi boxeo. Me llené la cabeza con mil dudas y mil suposiciones, pero al fin y al cabo todo es cuestión de tiempo. Después de mucho trabajo (mental y físico) me he vuelto a encontrar", dijo. Este verano ya subió a lo más alto del podio en los Juegos Mediterráneos de Taranto en los que se impuso a la argelina Fatiha Mansouri (4-1). Fuertes derribó la primera barrera para del boxeo femenino español en 2022, convirtiéndose en la primera en ganar una medalla en un Mundial. También fue la primera boxeadora nacional en clasificarse para unos Juegos Olímpicos. Ella compitió en los de París 2024, en los que cayó en primera ronda, pero abrió una puerta que espera que otras muchas mujeres atraviesen después de ella.

articles.title: Darren Till and Mike Perry finally look to settle decade-long UFC rivalry in February 2027
articles.summary: Darren Till and Mike Perry could finally settle their long-running rivalry in 2027. The former UFC stars have been linked with a fight for almost a decade.
articles.body: Darren Till and Mike Perry could finally settle their long-running rivalry in 2027. The former UFC stars have been linked with a fight for almost a decade. Their rivalry began after Till’s breakout win over Donald Cerrone at UFC Gdansk in October 2017. However, the bout never happened in the UFC.Now, the move to the Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship has brought the matchup back into focus. BKFC founder Dave Feldman has revealed that a Till-Perry fight could take place as early as February.Darren Till vs Mike Perry could finally happen in BKFCDarren Till joined Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship in April after signing a multi-fight deal with the promotion. Mike Perry has been competing in BKFC for the past four years. That has created a new opportunity for the two longtime rivals to finally share a fight.Dave Feldman confirmed that BKFC has already tried to make the fight happen. However, Perry currently has another plan in mind.When discussing Till’s return at BKFC 94 in Manchester, Feldman told SunSport, “We tried to make [the] Mike Perry [fight] happen. But then, you know, he’s trying to do something else right now. But I think that [fight] might happen in February. But Mike, he’s trying to do something else right now.”The February target could depend on Perry’s recovery. The 35-year-old suffered a shoulder dislocation during his most recent outing late last month. He could face at least four months on the sidelines because of the injury.That timeline could still allow Perry to return for a February fight. A potential training camp would also give him time to prepare for a clash with Till.Before that matchup can be made, Till has another major challenge ahead of him. The 33-year-old is set to headline BKFC 94 against former UFC middleweight Yoel Romero.The fight has attracted plenty of attention because of the age difference between the two men. Romero is 49, making him 16 years older than Till.Feldman also revealed that Romero was the one who asked for the fight.He said, “He [Yoel] asked for it, actually. He said, ‘I want the Darren Till fight.’ And then I went back to Darren Till and I said, [Are] you interested in Yoel?’ And he’s like, ‘Yeah, but I don’t know, he’s a little old. ‘Does it really do anything for me? And I said, ‘I think it does a lot for you.’ And then he’s like, ‘Yeah, let’s have it.’ ‘Let’s absolutely have it because people think I’m afraid of him, and I’m not. And let me show the world that I’m not.’”Till will now focus on Romero before potentially turning his attention back to Perry. A February meeting would finally give the pair a chance to settle a rivalry that began in 2017.The two fighters have taken very different paths since their first confrontation. Till became a UFC title challenger, while Perry established himself as one of BKFC’s biggest names. articles.title: UFC news: Gable Steveson breaks silence on 12-second knockout loss
articles.summary: On Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026, former Olympian and WWE star Gable Steveson faced off against Sean Sharaf at UFC 331. However, their match finished even before...
articles.body:
On Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026, former Olympian and WWE star Gable Steveson faced off against Sean Sharaf at UFC 331 . However, their match finished even before it properly started. Competing in his second-ever UFC fight, Steveson suffered a humiliating knockout loss against Sharaf.

Sharaf knocked out Steveson just 12 seconds into the first round. It marked Steveson's first loss in professional MMA , taking his win-loss record to 4-1. Before this loss, Steveson had won his first three fights against Braden Peterson, Kevin Hein, Hugo Lezama, and Elisha Ellison.

Following the loss, Steveson became a topic of conversation on the internet and a victim of severe social media backlash and trolling. Now, days after his loss, Steveson has broken his silence .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"This statement is for my family, my friends, my fans, and the people who truly know me and know the kind of man I am. I know there are people who will never support me, no matter what I say or do. That's their choice. But I'm speaking to the people who know me, not just as an athlete, but as a husband and a father to a young daughter," he shared.

Steveson also addressed the sexual assault allegations from a 2019 incident in his college years that resurfaced ahead of the fight. He claimed that it was raised to get into his head. He made it clear that he did not do any of the alleged things and was never charged with a crime as well.

"The allegations were not ignored nor brushed aside. They were thoroughly and heavily reviewed as I fully cooperated with law enforcement, including a separate Title IX review. There were no criminal charges, no conviction, and no finding of responsibility against me. The matter was closed, and there is no pending legal issue involving me. My own attorney did their own investigation and stated on the record that even if the law was changed, I would have the same outcome, which now speaks for itself," he added.

He also commented on how serioes allegations like these are. However, moving forward, he wants to stay focused on his wife, daughter, and his family. "To the people who support me, thank you. I know who I am. My family knows who I am. The people who have walked with me through life know who I am. That's what matters to me, and that's where I'm going to keep my focus.

"As for my opponent, congratulations. You caught me. A mistake on my end was made. It was your night. Just like my wrestling days after my loss, I came back with an undeniable will to win and focus that led me to the top of my sport. The result of Saturday night, I believe, will catapult me to do the same. I will be great, and this won't deny me," Steveson finished.

Steveson is a 2020 U.S. Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, a former WWE Superstar , and a member of the NFL's Buffalo Bills.

articles.title: Gaethje no parece interesado en una revancha con Ilia Topuria
articles.standfirst: El peleador estadounidense ha afirmado que no está pensando en un segundo combate contra 'El Matador' en este momento
articles.summary: El peleador estadounidense ha afirmado que no está pensando en un segundo combate contra 'El Matador' en este momento
articles.body: Justin Gaethje vive en una indecisión constante respecto a una posible revancha contra Ilia Topuria. El peleador estadounidense le arrebató el invicto y el cinturón de peso ligero a 'El Matador' el pasado 14 de junio en el UFC Casa Blanca, y desde entonces no ha parado de contradecirse en sus declaraciones. En su última aparición pública ha reconocido que no quiere pensar en un segundo combate contra el peleador hispanogeorgiano en este momento. Hace unos días, Topuria dijo que había vuelto a entrenar y que la próxima vez se aseguraría de que se revisasen mejor las guantillas de Gaethje. El peleador estadounidense entró al trapo de la provocación de 'El Matador' e incluso se mostró abierto a una posible revancha después de afirmar semanas antes que Ilia no se la merecía, pero ahora ha vuelto a cambiar su discurso de nuevo. En una entrevista en 'The Double Coverage Podcast', Gaethje ha sido tajante al respecto. "Ni siquiera quiero hablar de eso; o sea, puedo tener esta conversación contigo como aficionado a las MMA, pero no ahora mismo. Solo intento dejar que se curen el hematoma de la rodilla y la mano. Y luego volveré", sentenció. Justin ha reconocido que todavía no ha podido entrenar con normalidad porque las manos le siguen doliendo producto del combate con Topuria a pesar de que han pasado más de tres meses. Por tanto, no tiene pensado volver al octágono para realizar su primera defensa de cinturón hasta 2027. El pasado enero, Gaethje se convirtió en campeón interino por segunda vez en su carrera tras pasar por encima de Paddy Pimblett, y ante Topuria cumplió el sueño de toda una carrera al convertirse en campeón indiscutido del peso ligero en la Casa Blanca, el mejor escenario posible para hacer historia. De cara a su primera defensa tiene varias opciones sobre la mesa, aunque las más factibles son la revancha contra Topuria o un combate contra Arman Tsarukyan. De momento hay secretismo absoluto, pero está claro que tanto Gaethje como su equipo harán todo lo posible para evitar que sea 'El Matador' el encargado de recibirle de vuelta tras el descanso de ambos.

articles.title: Michael Pirotton vows to be the 'matador' when he fights 'money cow' Johnny Fisher at the Copper Box this Saturday
articles.summary: Johnny Fisher meets Michael Pirotton in a heavyweight clash this Saturday, live on Sky Sports; Pirotton appreciates he's an unknown, but is convinced he can use that to his advantage when they fight at the Copper Box Arena in London
articles.body:
The "Romford Bull" is hugely popular with an impassioned fan base, while his Belgian opponent is comparatively unknown.

But Pirotton is convinced he can use that element of surprise.

"I'm nobody in boxing," the Belgian told Sky Sports . "Nobody knows about me.

"That's my only advantage," he continued. "I know I'm supposed to lose.

"In the scenario I'm supposed to lose that fight. He's going to come full of confidence with his people and I know he's training hard. I have to be ready for whatever he brings. I'm going to be ready. I'm ready."

Fisher is a strong, come-forward fighter. "He's really aggressive and I can move. It's a classic heavyweight match-up. A bull against a matador. Let's see who wins," Pirotton said. "The horns in my belly, or if he ends up on the barbecue.

"The pressure is on his shoulders," the Belgian added. "He's just the money cow. He didn't grab anything he had. I know whatever happens I've grabbed everything I have."

He maintains the struggles he's faced in his career will help him outlast Fisher.

"They will find out. I don't brag before," Pirotton said. "But I'm confident. I don't brag before, I dance after, that's what I do.

"I'm glad for everything, that tough journey with some bad stuff happening to me. Because it enfused a deep sense of stoicism in me. What happens is going to happen and I'm still going to be Mike and I'm still going to be proud of what I do.

"I don't have a destination. I just have a path and I'm walking. I'm bleeding now but I keep walking and you're going to see."

Pirotton, who's never been dropped or stopped in his career, does have a warning for Fisher.

"I'm not over and it's not over until I say it's over and Johnny … he's a tough guy, he's strong guy, he's a decent guy, but he can't knock me out," he said.

"I'm able to punch. But I've never been able to punch like I'm really able to punch. And now I feel free to unleash my power."

articles.title: ‘Ruthless’ returns! Khamzat Chimaev vs. Robbie Lawler booked for Oct. 23 in Las Vegas

He's also got a considerable size advantage over Lawler, a common theme these days .

articles.title: European Boxing Championships: Great Britain's Chantelle Reid and Damar Thomas reach finals
articles.summary: Great Britain's Chantelle Reid and Damar Thomas will fight for gold at the European Boxing Championships after semi-final victories on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Great Britain's Chantelle Reid and Damar Thomas will fight for gold at the European Boxing Championships after semi-final victories on Wednesday.

Reid defeated Serbia's Milena Matovic 3-2 in her light-middleweight semi-final, while Thomas triumphed 5-0 over Azerbaijan's Mahammad Abdullayev in the men's super-heavyweight competition.

Team-mates Callum Makin and Dimeji Shittu are also guaranteed medals in the men's middleweight and light-heavyweight divisions respectively after victories in their quarter-finals.

Reid, the Commonwealth Games silver medallist, was behind after the first round against Matovic, but she was the unanimous winner of the second and did enough in the third to seal victory at Asics Arena Sports Hall in Sofia, Bulgaria.

"It was a really good bout. She's a really good girl and I hope we get to share the ring again one day," said Reid.

"On to the next. Each bout's gone better, each opponent's gotten better and I'll be boxing the best out of the weight category in two days' time."

The 28-year-old will face Busenaz Surmeneli in the final on Friday, after the Turkish boxer defeated Russia's Nadezhda Golubeva 3-2.

Thomas, the 21-year-old Commonwealth gold medal winner, will face Russia's David Surov in Friday's final after the Russian also completed a 5-0 victory over Austria's Ahmed Hagag.

Shittu, who had to settle for Commonwealth Games silver in August after a controversial defeat by India's Ankush Panghal, made sure of a European medal with a 5-0 win against Austria's Lucky Aimufua.

The 24-year-old will fight Russia's Cheerav Ashalaev on Thursday for a place in the final.

Itauma 'humiliated' but may never lose again - Hrgovic

"My first performance wasn't the best, but that's what I'm like, I go back to the drawing board and showed what I'm really capable of," said Shittu.

"Credit to my opponent. He was game, he was strong, but ultimately skills paid the bills, booked me a place in the semi-finals and a guaranteed medal.

"Last time I brawled, now I want to show that I can box. And the end of the day it's hit or not get hit. So I went out there, put on a show. Got the medal, let's go change that colour."

Makin, a bronze medallist at last year's World Boxing Championships, won 3-2 against Armenia's Marat Mikaelyan.

The 22-year-old will face Azerbaijan's Saidjamshid Jafarov in Thursday's semi-final.

The remainder of Great Britain's fighters experienced defeat on Wednesday, with Lauren Mackie and Amy Broadhurst both losing in the quarter-finals.

Commonwealth Games bronze medallist Mackie lost 5-0 to Lenka Bernadova of the Czech Republic in the women's bantamweight division, while Broadhurst was beaten 4-1 by France's Sthelyne Grosy in the women's lightweight.

Abdul Burton also represents Britain on Thursday, facing Turkey's Semih Gumus in the men's super-bantamweight semi-finals.

He and Shittu compete in the session starting at 11:30 BST, while Makin's bout with Jafarov is among the fights scheduled from 16:00.

articles.title: Moses Itauma: Briton 'humiliated', but may never lose again - Filip Hrgovic
articles.summary: Moses Itauma may never lose again if he can get over the "humiliation" of his IBF heavyweight title defeat, says Filip Hrgovic, who stunned the Briton in August.
articles.body:
Moses Itauma may never lose again if he can get over the "humiliation" of his IBF heavyweight title defeat, says Filip Hrgovic, who stunned the Briton in August.

The Croatian, 34, stopped Itauma, who had been the strong pre-fight favourite, in the ninth round of their meeting at the O2 Arena.

The early signs suggested Itauma had the measure of his opponent, with Hrgovic touching the canvas in the second round and conceding that he was "outboxed" early on.

Hrgovic took advantage when Itauma tired but stressed the 21-year-old southpaw is so skilful that he could go on to have a hugely succesful career if he learns from his loss.

"He's really good. He's special. Very fast, very talented and he countered whatever I tried with his speed and timing," said Hrgovic.

"I never was in the ring before with such a talented kid, with such a fast guy. You have some fast guys but they're small heavyweights. You can handle them with your power but this kid is fast and big. He's got great IQ and great talent.

"I'm still kind of angry because he outboxed me. In my whole career, in 20 years of boxing, I was never outboxed in any sparring or any fight."

While Hrgovic, who wants to unify the division, praised Itauma's boxing abilities, he suggested doubts remain over his mentality.

"It was big shock for him, big humiliation, so maybe it's end of his career if he's not mentally tough. If he recovers from this loss, mentally, it will be hard for anyone to ever beat him again," Hrgovic added.

"A lot of people after that kind of loss, they never come back. So, it will be a hard journey for him to come back.

"You have to go through a ruthless, hard training camp. You need to go through hell to be mentally ready for this. I think he was physically ready but it's the mental part."

articles.title: La rueda de prensa de WOW 32 Sevilla deja dos exclusivas clave para el futuro de la compañía
articles.standfirst: La promotora retransmitirá la cartelera de este sábado en el canal de Youtube de Cristiano Ronaldo en colaboración con el de MARCA, y ha asegurado que tiene un acuerdo con una plataforma de streaming y televisión líder a nivel global
articles.summary: La promotora retransmitirá la cartelera de este sábado en el canal de Youtube de Cristiano Ronaldo en colaboración con el de MARCA, y ha asegurado que tiene un acuerdo con una plataforma de streaming y televisión líder a nivel global
articles.body: Este sábado 26 de septiembre, WOW FC vuelve a la acción con WOW 32 Sevilla, una cartelera llena grandes nombres que dará inicio a un último cuatrimestre de año apasionante para la promotora española. Sin embargo, el show ya ha dado inicio este miércoles, con una rueda de prensa con público celebrada en el mítico Teatro Cervantes donde han formado parte los ocho peleadores que protagonizarán los cuatro combates principales de la cartelera y donde se han anunciado dos exclusivas clave para el futuro de la promotora. Nada más comenzar el evento, WOW FC ha anunciado que la cartelera de Sevilla de este sábado se retransmitirá en el canal de Youtube de Cristiano Ronaldo en colaboración con el de MARCA, por lo que se podrá seguir por ambos sitios. Además, también se ha sabido que la promotora ha llegado a un acuerdo con una plataforma de streaming y televisión a nivel global para futuras retransmisiones, además de diversos contenidos que no se centrarán únicamente en los propios eventos y podrán seguir potenciando el crecimiento de un deporte que no para de superarse. El atractivo principal de WOW 32 Sevilla será el combate estelar entre Sara Viéitez (3-2) y Hanna Palmquist (3-0), que se disputarán el primer cinturón de peso femenino de la compañía en la categoría de peso mosca. Durante la rueda de prensa, la peleadora española afirmó que "para mí significa mucho pelear frente a mi gente, este momento es muy especial para y voy a intentar que el cinturón se quede en España". De hecho, en el WOW Lisboa se convirtió en la primera mujer en recibir un bono de la noche, y este sábado puede seguir haciendo historia al ser la primera campeona de la historia de la promotora, en la categoría de peso paja. La peleadora sueca, mucho más fría, se limitó a decir que "este sábado voy a aplastar a vuestra estrella local". Por otro lado, Pepe Torres (10-1) regresa a WOW FC, y tiene muy claro su objetivo tras unos últimos meses complicados a nivel profesional. Su obsesión ya no es llegar a la UFC, sino disfrutar del proceso. "Mi objetivo sigue siendo la UFC, pero me quiero centrar en disfrutar cada día de lo que hago, de entrenar y de pelear. Ahora que he estado inactivo lo he echado de menos, por lo que me quiero centrar en el proceso. Si tiene que llegar UFC llegará, si tengo que triunfar en WOW FC así será, y mi objetivo es disfrutar de ello", sentenció, prometiendo espectáculo ante Jefferson Vargas (5-2). Daniel Ladero (4-3) y Przemysław Dzwoniarek (4-3) también estuvieron presentes y se mostraron muy respetuosos antes de un duelo que puede marcar el siguiente contendiente al cinturón de peso semipesado de WOW FC, mientras que Jeffry Batista (6-1) y Junior Hernández (6-1-1) prometieron dar espectáculo en el combate del pueblo e incluso el peruano afirmó que este enfrentamiento es serio candidato a llevarse el bono a mejor pelea de la noche. Este viernes se realizarán los pesajes oficiales, y el sábado se llevará a cabo el evento en el Polideportivo San Pablo que ya albergó WOW 18 en abril de 2025.

articles.title: European Boxing Championships: Damar Thomas reaches super-heavyweight final as Great Britain secure five medals
articles.summary: London super-heavyweight Damar Thomas beat Mahammad Abdullayev to reach the final of the European Boxing Championships in Bulgaria; Five GB boxers have guaranteed themselves European medals with Chantelle Reid winning through to the light-middleweight final
articles.body:
Thomas won his 90+kg semi-final against Azerbaijan's highly experienced Mahammad Abdullayev. The Londoner dominated all three rounds to win a unanimous decision.

Russia has returned to World Boxing competition and Thomas is due to box a Russian, David Surov, in Friday's final.

"Absolutely great. I'm just becoming who I thought I'd become and it would be great to win this," Thomas said.

"It's like a to-do list. I managed to tick off the Commonwealths and now the Europeans. And hopefully I can tick off Olympic gold as well."

Paris Olympian Chantelle Reid has also reached the final after beating Serbia's Milena Matovic in a fiercely contested bout.

The Serbian took a 3-2 lead at the end of the first round, but Reid responded with a 5-0 second round before edging the third to seal a 3-2 victory and reach the light-middleweight final.

She will face Turkish amateur boxing star Busenaz Surmeneli in the gold medal match.

"I was behind after the first round, but I just listened to my coaches, stuck to the game plan and got over the line," Reid said.

"Each bout has got better and so has the opponent. I'll be boxing one of the very best at my weight on Friday and I'm looking forward to it.

"It'd mean the world to me to win gold."

Dimeji Shittu (80kg), Callum Makin (75kg) and Abdul Burton (55kg) join them as GB boxers who have guaranteed themselves medals in Europe.

articles.title: Justin Gaethje reveals 'business decision' timeline for Arman Tsarukyan title fight
articles.summary: Justin Gaethje knows Arman Tsarukyan will be his next opponent – but there are key decisions to make first.
articles.body:
Justin Gaethje knows who his next UFC lightweight title opponent will be, but the timing remains in question.

Gaethje (28-5 MMA, 11-5 UFC) won the interim lightweight title by defeating Paddy Pimblett at UFC 324 in January. He followed that up by successfully unifying the title when he badly battered and left Ilia Topuria on the stool on the White House lawn at UFC Freedom 250 in June.

Since Arman Tsarukyan violently stopped Mauricio Ruffy at UFC 331, fans are eager to see that matchup as the next title fight. Gaethje knows Tsarukyan (24-3 MMA, 11-2 UFC) deserves a title shot, but the champ hasn't decided whether to defend the title or retire.

"Everyone's like, 'You f*cking fight Arman,'" Gaethje said on the "Flagrant Podcast." "I don't know what the f*ck – I have injuries I have to take care of. I haven't made a decision – but I am 37 years old. My first fight was in 2008. I've had 40 fights, including my amateur fights, so I don't know."

Both of Gaethje's title fights this year were MMA Junkie's Fight of the Month-winning wars that took their toll. Gaethje says he's still dealing with lingering injuries from his fight with Topuria. "The Highlight" was contemplating retirement before headlining the one-off spectacle in Washington DC, and he currently just wants time to think about his next move and make a decision after the holidays.

"It's not that I don't want to fight Arman, it really isn't," Gaethje said. "He's the next in line; if and when I defend this championship, that will be who I fight. I just don't know. Right now, I have a deep bruise in my knee. Still can't punch with my hand. We're three months removed from my last fight. I gave a lot of myself for this fight in January. In June, luckily I came out on top, but it cost me a lot, so I need to recover. I need to rest my brain because a lot of training went into those fights.

"I'm just going to enjoy being the champion for the rest of the year. I'm going to make a business decision and a life decision whenever the time comes."

Some online speculation suggests Gaethje is taking this stance as a negotiating tactic to squeeze more money from the UFC before accepting a fight against Tsarukyan. Gaethje was asked directly if he was posturing for a bigger payday, and he kept his answer concise.

"This has never been about money for me," Gaethje said. "It's about health."

articles.title: AEW Dynamite and Collision Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before All Out
articles.summary: Before we head to All Out this weekend, AEW gave us a special combined three-hour Dynamite and Collision as the go-home show.
articles.body:
Before we head to All Out this weekend, AEW gave us a special combined three-hour Dynamite and Collision as the go-home show.

Here's a look at what AEW advertised for Wednesday's show:

The New Level and Swerve Strickland vs. The Demand (Trios Titles)

Will Ospreay and Mike Bailey vs. Gabe Kidd and Claudio Castagnoli

Jon Moxley vs. Dezmond Xavier (Continental Title Eliminator)

Brawling Birds and Divine Dominion face-to-face meeting

Let's take a look at what happened on this week's combined Dynamite and Collision.

Swerve and New Level vs. The Demand (Trios Titles)

Dynamite opened up with the announcers running down the card for the night before we went to a backstage promo from The Demand. We also got a quick promo from Prince Nana, Swerve, Kofi and Austin Creed before both teams went to the ring for the opening contest.

The Trios Championships were on the line, and whichever team left Dynamite with the belts would head into All Out to defend against Adam Page and Brodido.

AEW has done a good job injecting some life into the trios division recently, and these two teams are a great representation of what this division can be if booked properly.

Swerve and Ricochet started the match by trading punches, but it didn't take long before they started incorporating some fast-paced offense. Swerve and New Level were especially efficient with some of their triple-team attacks.

All six men contributed to a fun match, but knowing what all of them are capable of, we couldn't help but feel like they were holding back a bit. The match was good, but it took a while before it felt like they were doing anything truly exciting.

The second half picked up quite a bit as the fight spilled out of the ring, but they ended up going a little too fast in some spots and made mistakes that stood out. Swerve and New Level secured the win to retain their titles after a fun final sequence.

Hangman and Brodido came out to confront the champions and hype their match for All Out.

Result: Swerve and New Level defeated The Demand

It's so easy to forget that Christian Cage was the reason Gates of Agony turned on Swerve.

Kofi and Creed have a different level of chemistry than most teams in AEW. Other than the Bucks, few duos have the kind of experience they have as partners. They can almost read each other's minds.

The Doomsday Device GOA used on Swerve looked good.

Kofi and Kaun had a very awkward spot late in the match. It was hard to tell what was supposed to happen.

The way Kaun set himself up for Swerve's double stomp from the apron looked way too contrived.

Xavier got a chance to earn a shot at the continental title this week when he took on Moxley in an Eliminator match. Due to the rules of the match, nobody else was allowed to be at ringside.

Xavier was giving up a lot of size and power, so it was surprising to see him engage in a lockup to start the match instead of using his speed to avoid it.

The first half of this was all Moxley. He was his usual aggressive self and didn't hold back against the Rascal one bit. It took until after the commercial break for Xavier to make any kind of headway.

While this match had some enjoyable moments, it never hit its stride. The predictability of the outcome was a factor, but there was a distinct lack of chemistry between the opponents until the last couple of minutes.

Moxley won by forcing Xavier to tap out to a sleeper. Marina Shafir showed up after the match and looked like she might attack Xavier, but he escaped unscathed.

Will Ospreay offered Mike Bailey a spot in United Empire during a backstage segment. Speedball accepted his offer.

Thekla gave a hilarious promo backstage.

Some of Xavier's strikes looked a little listless. He might have been worn out by that point in the match.

The Young Bucks, FTR, Christian Cage and Adam Copeland came out to hype their three-way title match coming up at All Out this weekend.

Stokely Hathaway said they were only there so they don't get fined by Tony Khan. The Bucks compared FTR to the Dudleys, which got a laugh from the crowd.

Cage made some jokes about everyone's moms until Copeland stopped him. All three teams talked some trash and dished out some insults, and it eventually broke down into a brawl.

A couple of security guards ended up getting taken out when they tried to take chairs away from Cope and Cage. The champions ended the segment standing tall.

This was pretty standard stuff. It was nothing groundbreaking, but they did their job hyping their upcoming bout.

Tommaso Ciampa made his way to the ring to battle Don Callis family member, Jake Doyle, before he faces Kazuchika Okada for the international title this weekend.

As soon as the bell rang, Ciampa went after Doyle in the corner. He kept the powerhouse off balance and tossed him out of the ring before nailing him with a big running knee right in the face.

This was designed to be a warm-up match for Ciampa, so there was no doubt that he would win, but he and Doyle did a great job making this fun even though we all knew who would win in the end.

Even though Doyle had a big size advantage, Ciampa never once felt like an underdog, which is a testament to how he has been booked to feel like a dangerous threat to just about anyone.

The Psycho Killer got the win, but he was favoring his shoulder after it was over. He issued a warning to Okada, which caused The Rainmaker to come out and respond.

Ciampa is great at hiding when he slaps his thigh for moves like his running knee strike.

Jake Something was a way more interesting name than Jake Doyle. It's too bad he can't use it in AEW for some reason.

The TBS Championship was up for grabs when Persephone defended the belt against Hyan. The champion's ally, Britt Baker, joined the commentary team.

Persy took control right out of the gate and almost got the pin, but the challenger stayed in the fight and started to make a comeback.

This was yet another match that felt pretty predictable, but they still made it feel competitive, especially once they had been going for a few minutes and had gotten comfortable with each other.

Persy is great at playing a bully because she is legitimately more powerful than most of the women on the roster, so it helped Hyan fall into the underdog role nicely.

Persephone cheated to win when she held the ropes for leverage during a pin, but the ref was oblivious.

It's nice to see Hyan getting some singles opportunities after Maya World was given such a strong push.

Baker was being pretty funny on commentary. She has fallen right back into being a great heel.

The newest member of United Empire teamed up with the world champion this week when Ospreay and Bailey took on Kidd and Castagnoli in tag team action.

Gabe and Claudio were not looking for a fair and competitive match. They went right after Ospreay and Bailey with malice. It took a couple of minutes before Speedball took Kidd down with a missile dropkick to turn the tide in his favor.

Speedball and Billy Goat both favor a fast-paced, high-flying style, so whenever they were in control, the match was more exciting. Whenever it was Kidd and Castagnoli, it felt more brutal.

This was a hard-hitting, competitive match that definitely outshone just about everything else on the show. This bout gave us a little bit of everything, so no matter what kind of wrestling you enjoy, the chances were good that you could see it here.

Ospreay got the win for his team by pinning Claudio with a Styles Clash.

Result: Ospreay and Bailey defeated Kidd and Castagnoli

Bailey was just added to United Empire tonight but he already has matching gear for the group.

The way Ospreay jumped onto the barricade, turned around and hit a flying forearm was awesome.

Moxley saying Castagnoli has countered every headscissor moments before he got taken down with one was hilarious timing.

Before they head to All Out to compete in a Street Fight for the women's tag titles, Divine Dominion and The Brawling Birds had a segment with Renee Paquette.

Megan Bayne and Lena Kross had a table brought out with tea and snacks as a gift for Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor.

It was meant to be kind of insulting, but Hayter and Windsor seemed excited to drink some tea and have some biscuits.

They ended up smashing the cups into Kross and Bayne's faces to start a fight. The former champions got the upper hand and bodyslammed both champions on the stage to end the fight.

This was short and sweet. It didn't need to be more than what it was, but some might see the segment as too simple at this stage in their feud.

Jack Perry gave a quick promo about facing Katsuyori Shibata at All Out.

The Outrunners vs. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight

Truth Magnum and Turbo Floyd were in action this week against the duo of Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight. Dalton Castle came out with The Outrunners, but he did not remain at ringside.

Even though The Outrunners are a good duo, this almost felt like a glorified squash. We all knew they were brought in to give Fletcher and Knight an easy win.

The match was entertaining for what it was, and it wasn't totally one-sided, but out of everything else on the show, this is the match that you could bet on the outcome and be right every single time.

Knight and Fletcher continue to look dominant as a tag team heading into their match against Steven Borden and Darby Allin this weekend. The Outrunners had a nice comeback in the second half, but they eventually fell to The Jet and Protostar when Knight pinned Floyd.

Result: Fletcher and Knight defeated The Outrunners

The Outrunners are such a fun team and they should be used more on AEW television.

Knight has really upped every level of his game. Even his strikes are looking crisper these days.

Mercedes Mone came out to watch Queen Aminata battle Skye Blue from the commentary table. Julia Hart accompanied Skye to the ring, and Mina Shirakawa was there with Aminata.

The last time these two tussled was almost a year ago in a tag team match, but it took them almost no time to find their groove.

Blue tried to be a bully early on, but Aminata made her pay for it with some stiff strikes. They were pacing themselves, but every move felt like it mattered.

Unfortunately, there was a little too much trash-talking going on at different times throughout the match, and it hurt the flow of the action in places.

The good news is they were not holding back and made every strike look brutal. The match didn't end until after the third hour in the show was up, and with one bout to go after this, we knew we were in for a long overrun.

Blue put up a good fight, but the Queen scored the win with a nasty running kick to the face. Julia and Mina got involved in the fight once the match was over. Thekla came in and gave the Sisters of Sin an unfair advantage, but Willow showed up to even the odds.

Chris Jericho came out before this match to give a promo. Nick Wayne joined him to talk about what happened the last time they were in the ring together. Wayne challenged him to a match at Grand Slam France.

Mone was wearing a protective face mask that was bedazzled to match her outfit.

Blue's suplex from the steps to the floor looked great. It was a brutal spot.

The main event of the night saw Pac take on Ace Austin in singles competition. The entire Bang Bang Gang came out but did not accompany Austin all the way to the ring.

In some ways, these men are carbon copies of each other. They are both short, muscular high-flyers who can wrestle you from the air or the mat. Pac had the edge in experience, but they were evenly matched in every other category.

This was a fantastic display of skill from two guys who don't often get the credit they deserve. Pac has always been known to be an incredible talent, but Austin is still new to many U.S. fans, so this was a good chance for him to impress some people.

Austin put up a good fight, but he was unable to kick out of the Black Arrow.

Juice Robinson dressing like a coach was pretty funny.

Austin doing squats with Pac on his shoulders was great.

The belly-to-belly suplex Pac used to throw Ace into the corner was awesome.

The special three-hour Dynamite and Collision ended up going closer to three and a half hours, but it felt like AEW made good use of the time.

Every match had something to offer, and most of the feuds that will make up the card for All Out were addressed directly or indirectly.

While Austin and Pac had a good main event, the best thing on the entire show was the tag match with Bailey and Ospreay taking on Kidd and Castagnoli.

The All Out card has the potential to be a great show, and Wednesday's episode did a good job selling it.

articles.title: Johnny Fisher: Deontay Wilder next? 'Good chance' it will be Dillian Whyte | 'It would be an honour'
articles.summary: Johnny Fisher believes he can set up a high-profile heavyweight clash with former world title challenger Dillian Whyte next, if he can overcome Michael Pirotton at the Copper Box Arena this Saturday; Watch Fisher vs Pirotton this Saturday live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The popular "Romford Bull" fights Michael Pirotton this Saturday at London's Copper Box Arena, live on Sky Sports .

Fisher is convinced him can put himself in the frame for a big-name opponent. He's been linked to Deontay Wilder but believes there's a "good chance" he'll fight former world title challenger Dillian Whyte next.

"Of course. Why not? That's a great name. It would be an honour. He's someone I looked up to when I was coming through the ranks," Fisher told Sky Sports .

"He's given us some great nights. I'm sure he would be a great bit of excitement for the Romford Bull Army."

He added: "That's a big name fight. These guys have had fantastic careers in their own right. There's no bones about the fact that they're coming to the ends of their careers. That's why it probably works proportionally to fight someone like me now. Because one, I've got a big profile but two, so have they.

"The appeal for me and my fanbase is fighting them guys because they've got bigger names, the Wilders and the Dillian Whytes. I've got a good chance of getting someone like Dillian Whyte, I really do think."

Fisher is a hard puncher, while former world champion Deontay Wilder is a famously hard hitter. Just the prospect of putting them together generates headlines.

"I've had a lot of people this week talking to me about fighting Deontay Wilder. Listen I would never call on that myself. I wouldn't be that disrespectful to someone of the level of Deontay Wilder," Fisher reflected.

"But of course I know the physicality and the physics of how heavyweight boxing works. If you connect as a 17.5 stone man on someone's chin, you've always got a chance and who am I to turn down an opportunity like that and not talk about it, because it's amazing."

Fisher is hoping to put on a more cultured display of his boxing when he fights Pirotton this Saturday. He's been working diligently with new trainer Tony Sims to that end.

"I'm a heavyweight boxer and first and foremost I'm an aggressive, front-foot, combination-punching heavyweight and I've got to do that and that's me," he said.

"I can refine that and add to that with what Tony's teaching me. But the big thing that Tony's speaking to me about is don't lose what you naturally are. Which is an aggressive come-forward fighter. We can add bits to it but you've got to be that.

"Physically I can use my dominant explosive self in a good way against him."

Watch Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton this Saturday live on Sky Sports .

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Cardiff to host heavyweight fight on 11 December
articles.summary: Cardiff's Principality Stadium will host Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury's all-British heavyweight fight on 11 December.
articles.body:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will contest their long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December.

The bout, more than a decade in the making, will be broadcast globally on Netflix.

BBC Sport understands the main event could take place in the early hours of Saturday morning in the UK, with organisers considering a late start to cater for audiences in the United States.

Joshua and Fury will come face-to-face at a news conference in London on Wednesday, 30 September, as the build-up begins to one of the most anticipated fights in British boxing history.

"I am inspiring a generation," Joshua, 36, posted on Instagram. Fury, 38, is yet to comment on the announcement.

The event is being promoted as a collaboration between Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and UFC chief Dana White.

"Two of the best heavyweights of this generation, finally in the ring together," Alalshikh said.

"This will be one of the biggest fights in boxing history. I am very happy to make this fight happen for the fans."

The former two-time world champions had already signed contracts for the bout earlier this year, but the date and venue had yet to be confirmed.

London's Wembley Stadium and New York's Madison Square Garden were the frontrunners to stage the fight, but both presented issues before Cardiff recently emerged as an alternative.

The Principality Stadium has hosted late-night boxing before, including Joe Calzaghe's fight with Mikkel Kessler in November 2007, which began at 01:00 GMT.

Welsh Rugby Union and Cardiff Council officials welcomed the fight, saying it would reinforce the city's reputation for staging major events and could bring a significant economic boost, although some operational details still need to be finalised.

Joshua had been pushing for the fight to take place in the UK and has got his wish.

"Forever indebted to the UK public for their support of Anthony Joshua. We couldn't have got this over the line without you," his promoter Eddie Hearn said.

It is notable that White, who fronts Zuffa Boxing, is involved in the promotion.

"For more than a decade, boxing fans have been clamouring for the heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Together, they bring 66 wins, 52 knockouts and multiple heavyweight world titles into the ring," White said.

"On December 11, two of the biggest heavyweights of this generation finally collide - and the winner will take a significant place in heavyweight history."

There was no official statement from Hearn or Fury's promoter Frank Warren in the official news release sent by Netflix. Hearn had previously said he did not want White to be involved in promoting the fight.

Could Fury-Joshua really take place in the early hours?

A major fight in Cardiff taking place in the early hours might seem unusual, but there is precedent for UK events being scheduled around American television audiences.

Ricky Hatton's career-defining victory over Kostya Tszyu at Manchester's MEN Arena in June 2005 began at about 02:00 local time, allowing US broadcaster Showtime to show the fight on Saturday evening.

Less than a year later, Welshman Calzaghe's unification fight against Jeff Lacy at the same arena was staged at a similar hour. Calzaghe's 2007 victory over Kessler in Cardiff was also influenced by the US television schedule.

Mixed martial arts has gone even later. Michael Bisping's UFC title defence against Dan Henderson in Manchester in 2016 began deep into the night, with the fighters making their way to the octagon at about 04:45 local time.

When the UFC returned to Manchester in 2024, the UFC 304 main card began at 03:00 BST - corresponding with its traditional 22:00 start on the US east coast, with Briton Leon Edwards fighting Belal Muhammad in the main event just after 05:30.

The precise timing of Fury-Joshua has yet to be announced and promoter Eddie Hearn has played down suggestions it could begin as late as 03:00 GMT.

A ringwalk around 01:00 or 02:00 GMT would place the fight at 20:00 or 21:00 respectively on the US east coast.

Years too late but Fury-AJ can leave a legacy - analysis

For years, British boxing has debated who would win, watched negotiations collapse and wondered whether Fury and Joshua would ever actually share a ring.

Now, finally, there is a date and a venue. It's happening.

In many ways, the uncertainty of recent weeks was the Fury-Joshua story of the past decade in miniature.

In 2020, the two camps agreed the basis of a two-fight deal. In 2021, contracts were signed for an undisputed heavyweight contest, only for Deontay Wilder's successful arbitration case to force Fury into a third fight with the American. Then, in 2022, Joshua accepted a 60-40 split to challenge Fury, but that attempt also fell apart.

Joshua gets the British fight he wanted, organisers are given a stadium capable of staging a huge event in December and broadcasters can tailor it towards American audiences.

There is also an intriguing subplot in White's involvement. While it does not necessarily tell us who wielded the most influence behind the scenes, his involvement underlines just how many powerful figures were involved in finally putting this fight together.

What matters most for supporters is that Fury-Joshua will happen in Britain. There are some fights that are about more than purses, broadcast deals and site fees. This is one of them.

British fans have followed every twist: the world-title wins, the defeats, the comebacks, the rivalries and, above all, the failed attempts to make this contest.

Now they will have the chance to travel to Wales and say they were there. Tens of thousands will descend on the Principality Stadium for what will be one of the biggest nights British boxing has staged in years.

And somewhere among them may be a youngster attending their first fight, watching two of Britain's most recognisable sportsmen make their walks to the ring and deciding they want to lace up a pair of gloves themselves.

The fight may have arrived years later than many wanted but Fury-Joshua can still leave that kind of legacy.

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: British heavyweight showdown set for Cardiff’s Principality Stadium on December 11
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury have finally agreed to fight in Cardiff on December 11 following a lengthy holdup over the location of their historic all-British heavyweight clash; Former world champions Joshua and Fury have been long-term rivals
articles.body:
The location of the fight had been a major stumbling block during negotiations for the hugely anticipated heavyweight clash.

Fury took to social media on multiple occasions to pin the blame for the delay on Joshua, before even touting a trilogy fight against Oleksandr Usyk, against whom both have lost twice, while Joshua's side had insisted the bout ought to be held in Britain.

"For 15 years no one has been able to make this fight. Back in April, I said that any announcement would come from me," Turki Alalshikh wrote on X.

"I can now confirm that Fury Vs Joshua will be coming to the UK, as I promised British boxing fans. The time for talking is over........"

But there was only ever one fight truly on the cards for them, with confirmation now coming that the heavyweight rivals will finally meet in arguably the biggest fight in British boxing history.

Joshua and Fury, both former heavyweight world champions, have had a long-running rivalry that's stretched over years, punctuated by callouts and trash talk but marred by the difficulty of finalising a deal.

Earlier this year the British boxing stars did sign to fight one another but months passed without a date or a venue being set. The wrangling intensified as taking the contest to New York's Madison Square Garden became a genuine possibility.

The fight appeared to be on the edge of collapse once again, with Fury threatening to seek alternative options.

But the all-British showdown has been salvaged and has now set a date for a UK stadium.

The Principality Stadium is no stranger to major UK boxing events. Joshua has fought there twice before, against Carlos Takam and in a unification with Joseph Parker. Historically, the all-British heavyweight super-fight between Lennox Lewis and Frank Bruno took place at the National Stadium in Cardiff, which preceded the Principality.

The main event is expected to start late at night due to international broadcasting considerations. But there is a precedent for that. Joe Calzaghe's 2007 fight with Mikkel Kessler took place at the stadium in the early hours of the morning.

As tortuous as negotiations for this super-fight have been, events in the ring also threatened to derail it.

Joshua's tune-up bout in July almost ended in disaster when little-known Kristian Prenga knocked him down twice in the first round. Joshua rallied to dispatch Prenga in the second round.

Fury's road to the fight has also been unusual. He announced his retirement after losing a rematch to Oleksandr Usyk and, after a year out of the sport, began training in Thailand. In April he came back at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London when he soundly outpointed Aslanbek Makhmudov.

He decided he wanted his own additional warm-up in July and boxed Mariusz Wach in Thailand in a non-TV bout, eventually stopping the veteran after seven rounds.

But the long journey towards Fury vs Joshua is now in its final stretch, set to end finally on December 11 in Cardiff.

articles.title: ‘I feel like fine wine’: 39-year-old Raoni Barcelos wants to shake up UFC bantamweight
articles.summary: Raoni Barcelos has been waiting almost nine years for a UFC main event.
articles.body: Raoni Barcelos has been waiting almost nine years for a UFC main event. When he finally gets one on Saturday, the 39-year-old Brazilian will share the cage with a fighter 18 years younger than him and ranked alongside him in the bantamweight division.Raul Rosas Jr. will headline UFC Fight Night at the Meta APEX in Las Vegas against Barcelos, with both men arriving on five-fight winning streaks. Rosas is 21 and ranked No. 12, while Barcelos has climbed to No. 8 in the latest Meta UFC rankings.For Barcelos, the main-event opportunity has been worth the wait.“I am very happy. It is a different feeling from the others because I am having my first main event after so long - almost nine years in the organisation. Having this opportunity is very great for me. I am taking advantage of it and living it in the best possible way,” Barcelos told TimesofIndia.com.“I am really happy with this moment. After nine years in the organisation, I am really enjoying all the time. I deserve this opportunity; I have deserved it for a long, long time, and I am really happy with that opportunity. So I want to give my best there.”Five rounds will be new to him in the UFC, but not entirely new to his career.“I think I've been through everything in the organisation. I've already lost by knockout, I've already lost by points, I've already lost and got robbed, and I've already won in many ways. I've already been through very bad situations. I've already fought five rounds. It wasn't in the organisation, but I've already fought five rounds and defended the title at the time of the RFA.“So these are things that I am now much more mature about. Facing Raul Rosas, who is only 21 years old, he still needs to go through some difficult things, and I think that's the big difference.”Five straight wins have changed the equationBarcelos' five-fight run includes wins over Payton Talbott, Cody Garbrandt, Ricky Simon and Montel Jackson. His most recent victory, a split decision over Jackson in April, extended the streak to five. Jackson dropped him early before Barcelos recovered and used his wrestling to get back into the fight.Rosas' most recent fight was also a decision win, against Rob Font in March. He is 6-1 in the UFC and has built his game around wrestling and grappling. He has also recorded six submission wins in his 13 professional victories.Barcelos said the preparation for his last two opponents has helped him develop in the same areas that could be important against Rosas.“The difference was the striking. Montel was a very aggressive guy, so I had to use a lot of my wrestling.“Against Ricky Simon, I knew he had very good boxing, but he also had very sharp grappling and was very strong on the fence. So they were two completely different camps, but during all these fights, I am getting stronger in my wrestling and my grappling.“About these two camps, first of all, Montel Jackson was a good striker, and I was working a lot on my wrestling. Ricky Simon was a very aggressive fighter, and he also had really good grappling. I have been training and getting better in my grappling game, so that's why I am getting better and better in every fight. That's why I am ready for this fight.”At 39, Barcelos wants the top fiveThe 39-year-old is now talking about the top five rather than simply trying to get back into the rankings. The current UFC rankings have him at No. 8, meaning a win over Rosas could put him within touching distance of the group he has been targeting.“I feel like fine wine, you know? I'm 39 years old, but I'm still young.“I'm still feeling young, you know? Training like I was 21 years old, and I feel good. So I don't know when I can say to you when I'm going to stop fighting, you know, when I'm going to continue to fight. But after this fight, I want to be in the top five guys.“I want to face those guys, and then 100 per cent, soon I want to get the title shot soon. But before that, I need to pass this guy and beat him and be in the top five ranking.”‘I’m the new guy’ in the bantamweight divisionThe timing gives the fight significance beyond the two places immediately beside their names. Barcelos does not see himself as an outsider to that group anymore.“I'm the new guy in the division. It's funny to say because I've been in the division for a long time and everyone knows me, but I'm showing that I can be among the best.“So that's my goal: to be fighting with them and to show more and more that this is possible.“Every fight here in the bantamweight division, they know me, and now I proved that I deserve to be where I am right now, and I want to continue there.“I'm the new guy in that division now. The top-five guys fight each other like this, but they need someone new, and I'm this new guy.”Watch UFC Fight Night - Rosas Jr. vs. Barcelos on September 27, 2026, from 5:30 AM IST live on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD & Sony LIV.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Se enfrentarán el 11 de diciembre en Gales
articles.body: La gran pelea de peso pesado que se debió hacer hace años, al fin ve la luz después de múltiples intentos. Anthony Joshua y Tyson Fury se enfrentarán el 11 de diciembre de 2026 en un duelo de excampeones británicos que tendrá lugar en Cardiff, en el Principality Stadium, y será retransmitido por Netflix. El promotor del boxeo Turki Alalshikh ha hecho oficial hoy que la denominada ‘batalla de Gran Bretaña’ se celebrará en el Reino Unido, tras semanas de tensas negociaciones. Hubo un tira y afloja tanto por la hora de inicio de la pelea –para garantizar la audiencia de EEUU- como por la ubicación de la misma. Finalmente se estima que los contendientes se dirijan al ring alrededor de la 01.00 de la madrugada (hora española). Joshua y Fury se verán las caras en una rueda de prensa en Londres el miércoles 30 de septiembre, dando el pistoletazo de salida a uno de los combates más esperados de la historia del boxeo británico. Recordemos que ‘Gypsy King’ viene de ganar en Tailandia a Mariusz Wach en un combate que no fue retransmitido, mientras que Joshua noqueó a Kristian Prenga en el segundo round, aunque el británico cayó dos veces en el primero. "Estoy inspirando a una generación", publicó AJ, de 36 años, en Instagram. Fury, de 38 años, aún no se ha pronunciado sobre el anuncio. Recordemos que ambos han vivido dos reinados distintos en los pesados y tienen en común que el último púgil que les arrebató el título mundial fue Oleksandr Usyk. “Durante 15 años nadie ha podido concretar esta pelea”, ha presumido Alalshikh en redes sociales, y ha rematado: “En abril dije que cualquier anuncio vendría de mí. Ahora puedo confirmar que Fury contra Joshua se llevará a cabo en el Reino Unido, tal como les prometí a los aficionados británicos al boxeo”. Por otro lado, el nombre de Manny Pacquiao ha sido asociado a esta cartelera en los últimos días. Aunque no hay nada concretado aún, se ha puesto encima de la mesa el nombre del filipino para que se enfrente al campeón del superligero Shakur Stevenson, una de las estrellas actuales. Esta pelea haría las veces de coestelar.

articles.title: Anthony Joshua could be in 'world of trouble' against Tyson Fury if he fails to improve on last performance, says Johnny Nelson
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury have finally agreed to fight in Cardiff on December 11 following a lengthy holdup over the location of their historic all-British heavyweight clash; Former world champions Joshua and Fury have been long-term rivals
articles.body:
On Thursday, the long-awaited all-British heavyweight clash was finally confirmed for December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium.

Joshua comes into the fight on the back of a major scare during his July victory over Kristian Prenga, with the 36-year-old knocked down twice in the opening round before stopping his unheralded opponent in the second.

The fight was Joshua's first since he survived a December 2025 car crash that claimed the lives of his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Adodele.

Former cruiserweight world champion Nelson told Sky Sports News : "Well mentally, remember almost a year ago, AJ was involved in a horrific accident.

"That's a lot to get over and get his head around. Hopefully, he's in a great space with that.

"His last fight didn't represent him very well. If you're going on his last fight, he's in a world of trouble."

Having taken time out of the ring after his two 2024 defeats to Oleksandr Usyk, Fury has this year recorded comfortable victories over Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach.

Nelson continued: "You look at Tyson Fury, his last fight was underwhelming but it wasn't worrying.

"So, the stages they're at, if you're going by their last fights, the one that's in a better condition I'd say would be Tyson Fury, because his last fight read better than AJ's last fight."

Nelson explained that he believes Joshua (30-4) has experienced a bigger drop-off than Fury (36-2-1) due to the former's greater reliance on his athleticism.

"Without a doubt, Joshua is explosive," Nelson said. "You saw the fights when he boxed people like Francis Ngannou, took them out cold.

"Tyson Fury, we've seen him box and knock people out. We've seen him go the distance. We've seen that slow burn and him winning a fight.

"With AJ, it just seems that he stands out more for the knockouts than his boxing ability, even though he does have boxing ability.

"Whereas Tyson Fury, it wouldn't surprise you if he boxes his way around the ring for 12 rounds because he has that ability.

"Is AJ going to produce a crash, bang, wallop? Most people would probably be saying if it stops early inside the distance, you'd say AJ because of that explosive power.

"If it goes the distance or it's a late stoppage, you'd say Fury because he has the boxing intelligence, IQ and success of stopping people late."

'They'll bring the best out of each other'

Nelson is confident that despite both being past their prime, the long-standing rivalry between Fury and Joshua will ensure they bring the best out of each other.

"I think both fighters, not just AJ, are way past their best," Nelson added.

"But I also believe that because they're fighting each other, if there's ever a time that they're going to be able to turn back time for one night only, it's December 11. That one night is when they get everything.

"They understand that one mistake ruins their Christmas, ruins their New Year, ruins this beef that they've had forever and a day.

"There's a lot at stake for both fighters. They are not at their best, they're not the fighters they were, but the fighters they are today match each other perfectly, and they'll bring the best out in each other."

articles.title: Aleksandre Topuria se enfrentará a Santiago Luna en el UFC Qatar el 21 de noviembre
articles.standfirst: 'El Conquistador' vuelve al octágono tras un año de inactividad para enfrentarse a otro de los grandes prospectos del peso gallo
articles.summary: 'El Conquistador' vuelve al octágono tras un año de inactividad para enfrentarse a otro de los grandes prospectos del peso gallo
articles.body: Aleksandre Topuria (7-1) está de vuelta. Lo que era un secreto a voces ya es una realidad, y MARCA ha podido saber de primera mano que 'El Conquistador' volverá a subirse al octágono en el UFC Qatar del próximo 21 de noviembre para medirse a Santiago Luna (8-1), otro de los grandes prospectos del peso gallo que llevaba bastante tiempo pidiendo un combate contra el peleador hispanogeorgiano. Desde hace unos días se comentaba que este combate podría darse en Doha dentro de unas semanas, y finalmente Aleksandre ha recibido la oferta por parte de la UFC y ha aceptado un combate que le puede dejar a las puertas del top 15 de la categoría, ya que sería en caso de ganar sumaría tres victorias en menos de dos años en la promotora de MMA más importante del planeta. Para ello tendrá que superar a un peleador con un brillante futuro por delante, con una gran pegada y una buena base en lucha. Luna irrumpió con fuerza en la UFC en septiembre de 2025 finalizando a Quang Lee, y en febrero de este mismo año superó a Ángel Pacheco para mantener el invicto. Sin embargo, el pasado junio recibió un duro correctivo por parte de Bryce Mitchell y fue sometido en el tercer asalto, lo que frenó en seco sus aspiraciones. Aleksandre se centró en la primera mitad de año en ayudar a su hermano Ilia para el UFC Casa Blanca, pero ya está preparado para regresar por todo lo alto. "Aleksandre Topuria, te quiero a ti en la siguiente", dijo Luna después de su victoria en el UFC México ante Pacheco. Pues bien, ya tiene lo que buscaba después de meses insistiendo. La última aparición del mayor de los hermanos Topuria fue precisamente en el UFC Qatar de 2025, cuando se impuso a Bekzat Almakhan con una brillante actuación que le dio la victoria por decisión unánime. Previamente a eso había superado en su debut a Colby Thicknesse en febrero de 2025, por lo que este combate será clave para conseguir un rival rankeado en su siguiente pelea. De hecho, el ganador de este enfrentamiento dará un paso de gigante en una división llena de grandes nombres en el top 15. Aleksandre tiene 30 años y Luna 22, por lo que la experiencia puede ser un grado en una pelea donde ambos pueden manejarse bien tanto en el suelo como en el striking. Sin duda, un enfrentamiento candidato a llevarse el bono a mejor pelea de la noche teniendo en cuenta sus habilidades.

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: AJ has devastating power to end it but smart money's with Fury, says Johnny Fisher
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua look to end their long-running rivalry when they box on December 11 at the Principality stadium in Cardiff; Heavyweight contender Johnny Fisher gives his verdict on the fight; Watch Fisher take on Michael Pirotton this Saturday live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Rivals for years, Fury and Joshua had to fight, though it's taken almost 10 years for it to eventually come to fruition.

They will now box at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11.

Johnny Fisher is looking to cement his own rise up the heavyweight rankings when he fights Michael Pirotton on Saturday, live on Sky Sports .

A former sparring partner of Fury's, Fisher has welcomed the all-British super-fight. He appreciates the impact it'll have on UK boxing.

"We've been talking about this fight for a decade now and it's finally over the line. The Principality is going to hold it, so it's exciting," Fisher told Sky Sports News .

"AJ and Fury transcend the boxing community. Everyone in England who knows the sport knows the names so it's going to be massive for the sport of boxing."

As well as protracted negotiations to make the fight, Fury and Joshua both had to get through warm up bouts to set up this clash.

Coming back to boxing after a terrible car accident, Joshua had a stuttering performance against Kristian Prenga in July when he hit the canvas twice in the first round before stopping his opponent in the next.

Fury briefly retired after losing two fights to Oleksandr Usyk but returned this year to beat Arslanbek Makhmudov in London and Mariusz Wach in Thailand.

While Fury is deemed to be the more in-form fighter, Fisher warned: "AJ has got that devastating power to end it whenever he needs to.

"Going on the last six months to a year of performances, Fury has dusted off that ring rust and the same with Mariusz Wach when he fought him, while AJ has been in a bit of jeopardy when he fought Kristian Prenga so the smart money is with Fury right now but who knows? That's why we're going to tune in."

There are other areas of comparison with common opponents. Both boxed Francis Ngannou in recent years, with Fury edging out the UFC fighter whereas Joshua rapidly levelled him.

"There's been points when I think Fury has been ahead of the game a few years back but then I thought AJ with that knockout of Francis Ngannou," Fisher said.

"Fury didn't have the performance that we thought he would against Ngannou, but then in recent times I would back Fury.

"As boxing fans we now get to deliberate and debate and see all the platforms talking about it."

articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Both fighters to earn British record paydays for Cardiff clash, says promoter Frank Warren
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury have finally agreed to fight in Cardiff on December 11 after a lengthy delay over the venue for their historic all-British heavyweight clash; Fury's promoter Frank Warren shared new details of the negotiations with Sky Sports News
articles.body:
The long-awaited all-British heavyweight showdown was finally confirmed on Thursday as the date and venue - Cardiff's Principality Stadium - were announced by the fight's promoters.

It was also reported by Ring Magazine that the WBA world title will be on the line, giving both Fury and Joshua the opportunity to become three-time world champions.

Despite both fighters having signed to face each other, the fight was in major doubt amid a dispute over the location before Cardiff was agreed upon as the host.

Warren, Fury's long-time promoter, told Sky Sports News : "They're getting paid more than any British fighter has earned in a fight ever.

"That's why no one could walk away from it because of the amount of money involved. From Tyson's position he really, really wants this fight.

"The money was agreed ages ago. The sticking point was that the contracts did not match up and neither side was aware of that. There were two different venues that were put in the contract.

"The bottom line of it is, everyone has compromised and it's on now."

Ring Magazine's Mike Coppinger reported on Thursday evening that the fight will be for the WBA 'super' heavyweight title vacated by Oleksandr Usyk, who beat both Fury and Joshua twice on his way to becoming undisputed champion.

Murat Gassiev had been elevated to WBA primary champion as the holder of the organisation's 'regular' title, but will be demoted by the decision to put the 'super' title on the line for the all-British bout.

While Fury has been given primary billing with his name first on the fight announcement, Warren revealed that it has yet to be decided which of the pair will walk to the ring first.

A challenger would usually be first to walk to the ring, where they would then have to wait for the champion to follow.

But given neither of the former world champions currently holds a title, the order of the ring walk is one of many elements that will continue to be negotiated.

On Fury's name coming first on the promotional materials, Warren said: "The billing says Fury-AJ. I think it's quite right because Tyson is ranked higher than AJ in all the governing bodies' rankings, and alphabetically, he should come first anyway."

And on the ring walks, he added: "That's all to be decided. Being realistic about it, all that sort of stuff, spin a coin, whoever wins, wins.

"As long as they're in the ring for the first bell, that's all that matters.

"For me, Tyson should come in second because he's the guy who's ranked highest in all the governing bodies."

'Fury can make it as easy as he wants to'

Warren is extremely confident that Fury will emerge victorious, but did warn that "you can't dismiss" Joshua due to his power.

"I have very strong feelings about how the fight will end," Warren said. "I genuinely feel he [Fury] can make it as easy as he wants to.

"You can't dismiss AJ because he's a big, big puncher and in his last fight he was in trouble, but he pulled it out the bag with his punch power, but Tyson is a much different opponent, and you know he's got a good chin.

"What I class as a good chin is when guys go over, get up off the floor and come back. Tyson has done that. He's a tough, tough customer. He's very confident, and his boxing ability will prevail in the end. He'll come out with the prize.

"These guys have been talking about this fight for 12 years - maybe even longer - and everything will have to be on the line. Neither of them will want to lose.

"Tyson feels he's got AJ's number. I think he wins and I think he'll do it in spectacular style."

articles.title: European Boxing Championships: Abdul Burton reaches final after bronzes for Callum Makin and Dimeji Shittu
articles.summary: Abdul Burton reaches the men's super-bantamweight final after Callum Makin and Dimeji Shittu claim bronzes at the European Boxing Championships.
articles.body:
Great Britain's Abdul Burton joined team-mates Chantelle Reid and Damar Thomas in reaching finals at the European Boxing Championships in Sofia, Bulgaria.

Burton, 20, comfortably beat Turkey's Semih Gumus 4-1 in the men's super-bantamweight semi-final.

He will face Russia's Viacheslav Rogozin in Friday's final, when Reid and Thomas will be contesting for the women's light-middleweight and men's super-heavyweight titles respectively.

"I'm happy, it was a good performance against a tricky kid," said Burton.

"I had to stay disciplined. I've really enjoyed the week, it's good to secure silver but I'm going to be pushing for gold tomorrow. It would be pretty big to do that in my first major, when I'm this young, so all eyes on that."

Burton was one of three British semi-finalists but the only winner after Dimeji Shittu and Callum Makin were both beaten and claimed bronze.

Commonwealth Games silver medallist Shittu suffered a 4-1 defeat by Russia's Cheerav Ashalaev in the light-heavyweight division, while Makin lost by the same scoreline to Azerbaijan's Saidjamshid Jafarov at middleweight.

"He was a strong opponent, it was competitive but fair play to him," said Shittu.

"He's a tough guy, big scary guy - but I'll 100% get him next time. I've still come away with a medal so I'm delighted with that. It wasn't to be today but I will learn from it and come back."
